scope: 制备、组装、发电测试、Fig.4应用与解释边界
fabrication: DLP 405 nm; 98 wt% PEGDA and 2 wt% BAPO; 50 micrometre layers; 8 seconds per layer
FCC-like open lattice; partially carbonized at 350 degrees Celsius for 4 hours under inert atmosphere; scaffold retained
Separate p-Sb2Te3 and n-Bi2Te3 thermal evaporation at room temperature; film thickness about 1 micrometre
Ten p/n pairs electrically connected in series using nickel contacts and Ag-Sn solder, between insulating ceramic plates; assembly heat treatment at 220 degrees Celsius
applications_verified: Planar resistive heat source with air natural cooling; load tests at temperature differences 20, 40, 80 and 120 degrees Celsius; reported maximum about 1.4 microwatts
Circular thermoelectric structure mounted on alumina hot-air pipe; main text reports temperature difference 120 degrees Celsius and maximum power 3.2 microwatts
LED demonstration through LTC3108 power circuit; article explicitly mentions stored energy
scientific_boundaries: Figure caption panel letters contain mismatches; explain panels by the verified actual figure and main text
Pipe heat-source temperature is 150 degrees Celsius in main text page 7 but 300 degrees Celsius in Methods page 8; preserve discrepancy
Do not associate the approximately 10 percent efficiency point in Fig.4i with the 120 degrees Celsius power-test condition
Efficiency is calculated using Pmax=Voc^2/(4Ri), Qout=kappa*A*DeltaT/L and eta=Pmax/(Pmax+Qout); it is not a directly measured whole-system heat balance
LED demonstration does not establish continuous lighting; LED current, duration, storage capacity and precharge state were not verified
Human-body wearing, vehicle exhaust and chimney installation were not experimentally demonstrated in the checked paper
Microwatt-level power and high source resistance require power-circuit startup and impedance matching verification before reproduction
supplement_status: Supplementary file links were located, but files were not read successfully in this turn; do not infer their absent contents.
lab_adaptation: Existing 3D printing and Sb2Te3/Bi2Te3 magnetron sputtering provide a candidate adaptation. Printer type, scaffold thermal stability, interior coating continuity, film composition, Seebeck sign and electrical resistance need verification.
